methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in AI & Software (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in AI & Software, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
General Intuition, a software and AI company founded by Pim De Witte, presents a valuation challenge due to limited stage-specific comparables. The analysis draws on a peer universe of nine companies in the AI & Software sector: one public (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and eight private firms including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition.

The peer-median method proves inapplicable here. Despite identifying twelve same-sector peers within AI & Software, none meet the filtering criteria for stage alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, or similar valuation tier. Zero datapoints survived the narrow filter thresholds (minimum three required), making an all-sector median uninformative and potentially misleading given the heterogeneity of AI & Software valuations across seed through growth stages.

The absence of sufficient stage-specific and tier-comparable peers means triangulation cannot be completed with confidence. A defensible valuation range cannot be supported by the current dataset without either expanding filter criteria (risking apples-to-oranges comparisons) or introducing additional methodologies—such as discounted cash flow or revenue multiple analysis—for which underlying financials were not provided. Further data collection on General Intuition's revenue, growth rate, and capital deployment, along with clarification of its development stage, is necessary to anchor a credible valuation.
